      public Optional<org.knowm.xchange.dto.Order> getResultOrder()
      Returns the resulting order built from the exchange-specific result. Lazily constructs the result order on first access via the abstract buildResultOrder() method, which is implemented by each exchange-specific subclass to parse the response into a standard Order.
      Returns:
      the result order if the execution was successful, empty otherwise

    • rejected

      public boolean rejected()
      Whether the exchange itself refused this placement, as opposed to the request failing without any answer coming back. Only a refusal proves the order does not exist: a transport failure leaves its existence unknown — the exchange may well have accepted the order and only the acknowledgement got lost — and an order that may exist must never be placed again blindly.

      Classified by error type: an IOException is a transport failure, since a client that received and parsed an answer reports it as an exchange-level error instead. Exchanges whose client reports refusals as I/O errors have to override this.

      Returns:
      true if the exchange answered this placement with a refusal

    • getRejectedOrder

      public Optional<org.knowm.xchange.dto.Order> getRejectedOrder()
      The order state to record for a placement the exchange refused: the submitted order stamped REJECTED, a final status, so a caller can tell "the exchange said no, nothing exists" apart from "no answer came back and the order's existence is unknown" (which carries no order state at all). Empty unless this result is a refusal — see rejected().
      Returns:
      the refused order snapshot, or empty if this result is not a refusal

    • getAcknowledgedOrder

      public Optional<org.knowm.xchange.dto.Order> getAcknowledgedOrder()
      The exchange's acknowledgement of a successful placement, as an order snapshot carrying the id it assigned and the status it reported. Recording it gives the execution its exchange-side identity at placement time rather than at the first order event — without which an execution whose events never arrive cannot be looked up on the exchange at all. Prefers the exchange-built result order when that already carries the assigned id, and otherwise stamps the id and status onto a copy of the submitted order.
      Returns:
      the acknowledged order snapshot, or empty for a failed or unidentified placement
